main_text.p: etiam cum in clericorum ordine erat, & postea cum Antiochia diuina gubernacula suscepit, Dei Pontificem, & comministrum habet, & nuncupat, & ijs, qui non ita tenent, aduersatur. Et infra: Et sanctissimus quoque Elias, qui nunc Hierosolymorum praesul constitutus est, in omnibus Theodosij praecessoris sui vestigijs insistens, nunquam aduersus sanctissimum Patriarcham petulantijs communicauit, sed eos etiam, qui Saracenorum Apocrisiarij, & illius personam mentiti fuerant, anathemate ferijt. Et Actione quinta: Οἱ τοποτηρηταὶ τῆς ἀποστολικῆς [?] θρόνων εἶπον. τῷ δὲ ἡ ἁγία [?] τῆς Ἱεροσολύμων Ἐκκλησία, ἥπερ τῆς [?] Ἀντιοχέων, καὶ Ἀλεξανδρέων [?] ἀδιάπτωτον ἀπέβαλεν, [?] μὴ [?] ἴχνη αὐτῶν [?] τέκνον. [?] τὸν ἁγιώτατον Φώτιον [?] ἐνομολογούμενον, καὶ [?] Πατριάρχην Κωνσταντινουπόλεως [?]. Locumtenentes Orientalium Sedium dixerunt: Nanque sancta Hierosolymitana Ecclesia, nec non Antiochena, & Alexandrina nunquam reiecit, aut infitiata est sese reputare sanctissimum Photium quammaxime legitimum, & secundum Canonum statuta electum Patriarcham Constantinopolitanum, ex quo in sanctam hanc sedem proiectus est:

page.notes: The Greek passage in the Actio quinta is only partly legible in the scan; every doubtful Greek word is marked [?] and may be wrong in its letters or accents. The Greek line of the Actio begins with "Οἱ τοποτηρηταὶ", and the closing Latin sentence runs on from it on the same line. The paragraph is treated as one because no indent separates the Latin and Greek lines. The first word "etiam" continues from the previous page. No running head, catchword or marginal notes are printed on this page.
